messages:
support-jane: FYI customer reported a wave of 503s when Dedicated tried to fail over from eu-west to us-west. They hit our API and saw 429 then 503s, app-level timeouts. Raising for triage.
ops-oncall: Which customer and which pool? any recent config changes?
support-jane: customer=acme-inc, dedicated-pool=eu-prod-2, requested cross-region evac during scheduled maintenance window. No manual config changes noted.
eng-alex: I pulled logs — placement service returned errors: 
```
{"error":"allocation_failed","reason":"no_available_gpus"}
```
Then a cascade where our fallback runner attempted to route to us-west and got auth failures against account billing: 
```
HTTP 401 {"error":"billing_auth_failed","code":"account_key_revoked"}
```
sre-carla: 401 from billing? That would prevent claiming capacity in target region leading to 503s. Is this per-tenant or global?
support-jane: Looks tenant-scoped. Acct-bob confirmed renewal payment hit a transient processor decline and our KMS rotated the customer key earlier this week (housekeeping note).
acct-bob: We saw a payment provider transient between 15:02-15:08 UTC, some retries succeeded. Not sure why the key rotation impacted auth at 15:12. filing with billing infra.
infra-bot: autoscaler: triggered scale-down eu-prod-2 at 15:00 -> scale-up blocked at 15:11 due to allocation errors. fallback routing to us-west initiated at 15:12.
eng-alex: Repro steps I ran locally: 1) mark eu-prod-2 drained; 2) post 50 concurrent requests with token for acme-inc; 3) observe placement errors then billing 401 on claim. curl snippets: 
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/alloc -d '{"region":"us-west"}'
# -> 401 {"error":"billing_auth_failed"}
```
ops-oncall: Short-term mitigation: can we force soft-failover to a warm standby pool that doesn't require billing claim (internal fallback) so the customer doesn't see 503s?
sre-carla: We can flip route to warm-standby-us-west-1 for acme-inc (manual override) to bypass per-tenant claim for ~30m. Doing that now.
ops-oncall: Also suggest temporarily increasing per-tenant burst quota for acme-inc while billing resolves. eng-alex can you confirm any risk of noisy neighbor if we widen quota?
eng-alex: Warm standby has isolation (capped vCPU/GPU slices) so risk is low for a 30m window. Main concern is KV cache cold start — latency will spike for first few requests. Communicate to customer.
support-jane: Noted. Messaging customer: "we're routing you to warm standby in us-west while we resolve a billing auth hiccup; some requests may be slightly slower as caches warm." They asked for ETA.
acct-bob: Working with payments team, expected resolution 20-30m. I'll post updates.
sre-carla: Postmortem action items: 1) add circuit-breaker so billing auth failures don't block region failover; 2) add churn guard to prevent concurrent KMS rotations during maintenance windows; 3) surface per-tenant billing health in console.
eng-alex: I'll draft a rollout for the circuit-breaker change. Minimal patch: treat billing 401 on allocation as non-fatal if warm-standby capacity is available, and log an alert to finance.
support-jane: Customer acknowledged and is muted for now. I'll update when billing confirms. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open until billing confirms or we've validated normal traffic for 30m.
infra-bot: monitor alert created: incidents/1931245000 - standby-route-engaged for acme-inc
acct-bob: payment provider reports resolved at 15:40 UTC. I'll confirm our billing token refresh succeeded.
sre-carla: Verified traffic now flowing to primary pools after manual transition back. No further 503s in last 5m. Closing in 20m unless regression.
support-jane: Closing note: customer thanked for quick response. Will include notes in the ops follow-up doc."
